title: Freddie Blackburn, the Gene Krupa record and the knife
summary: Freddie drank, played along to a Krupa record, and during a number Bill Kurzie pulled a bowie knife to calm him before both were drafted.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I said, well, I'm -- I ain't getting all those dollars up there and I can't drink all my Mol$en (phonetic) and, but, speaking of Freddie.
One time there was a -- Freddie was Freddie.
We had a jukebox on at intermission that had Gene Krupa on the jukebox. Freddie would listen to this record for 20

minutes then one night he says, you know Jacques, that man can't do nothing with me. I'm going to show you. He played the record, he got up on his drums and played with the record. He said, now, you see? You see what I did to him, don't you? I said, yeah, Freddie, you got it.
He said, come on, have some of this, and I said, "No, Freddie, I know you love that better than me."
Come on, I'll buy you some beer, here -- give him what he want -- glug, glug, glug, glug, glug.

Now, Freddie is up there frantic. So, now, we are playing and Freddie was up there trembling and, trembling like a dog, making away with some bones -- and you know how a dog does, he was shaking and going on and Bill said, well, let's play something, Freddie said man, let's play something fast because that boy out there, had a boy named Willie Jones come up there one time and ate Freddie up.

And I clapped my hands -- Freddie said, I'm going to kill you. I thought you was my friend but you liked that man there, the way he was playing and I said, Freddie, I'm just clapping for professional reasons, you know. But I think you like him. I says, naw. I don't like him that much you my man. All right, then. Okay, now, be careful.
So, they's starting the number off, I think it was "I'm Gonna Sit Right Down and Write Myself a Letter" -- da, da

dee, dee --Freddie picked up, thrump da, thrump da, da baa, And Freddie, "I'll take out my silver and cut your head off." be da, -- Bill said, "Freddie, I warned you about that. Go to hell then, and he was up, Bill pulled out a bowie knife or something and Freddie, said, Freddie if you come down here I will not allow you to go back up there. I will not allow you to go back up there.
Now, it seems though the reason why Bill was up he had cut somebody's head off and I didn't know that.

I said, Freddie, Freddie, (foreign sentence) -- I said, come on, we gonna play the "Bugle Blues," da, da, dee dum thrump pa --Freddie went (inaudible) up there, Freddie went crazy up there with his hands and said you know -- Bill makes me mad sometimes. He'd better stop playing with me.
Yeah, Freddie, yeah, Jacques loves you.
And then, Freddie said, "Bill, didn't you have that there for me?" "I speck I did, Freddie. You was getting awful rought up there and I had to calm you down."

Boy, that was the -- and so, well, now, all these people started evenings and going to service. And then, Rock-head had no musicians up there. He had to go put a jukebox up there. Everybody said, and so, Bill, his job was, he was in the army and he was marching all them people to the ships.
He was in the band. He was marching them to the ships man, then Freddie, I think, Freddie, they put him into the tank corps right away.
